Use case: style-transfer.
Image 1 is the edit target: a healthcare system illustration for a professional machine-learning portfolio.
Change the visual language to a restrained FLAT 2D EDITORIAL TECHNICAL ILLUSTRATION. Retain the subject relationships: clinical folders/structured records and clinical notes on the left, secure HPC and ML computation in the center, risk prediction and evaluation workstation on the right, connected by fine data lines.
Style: crisp vector-like shapes, precise thin navy outlines, simple solid color planes, natural proportions of engineering equipment, warm ivory background, dusty blue and sage with small lavender and terracotta accents. Flat printed illustration with plenty of whitespace and high legibility. A slight three-quarter view of equipment is fine, but use no simulated material depth.
Remove all toy/clay aesthetics: no 3D rendering, bevels, glossy surfaces, gradients, volume lighting, cast shadows, rounded toy proportions, decorative beads, cartoon characters or cute faces. No enclosing module boxes, flowchart panels or numbered steps. Devices remain recognizable physical objects rather than generic rectangles.
Text: only three clean English labels: "Clinical data", "Secure HPC", "Risk evaluation". No other text, performance numbers, equations, logos or watermarks.
Wide 3:2 composition. Keep the connected system concept clear.

Subject: Low-Latency LLM Inference on Heterogeneous Edge Devices.
Scene: A professional distributed inference system: two recognizable Jetson-style single-board edge computers grouped on the left, three smaller Raspberry-Pi-style gateway boards in the middle, and a GPU server on the right. A few short lavender model-layer tiles sit beside the edge boards and server to represent partitioned transformers. A small flat scheduling dial above the gateways connects with fine amber control lines to the hosts. Thin blue data connections and a green return connection show asynchronous requests and responses. Use natural circuit-board proportions, visible flat chips and ports, no brand logos. Do not imply that these physical objects are an exact photographed deployment topology.
Text: only three short English labels along the bottom: "Edge devices", "Async gateways", "GPU server". No extra text, numbers, equations or numerical performance figures.
